maria: quick dump from this morning's A100 vs H100 pass across several open 7B-family models :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: TL;DR — H100 gives ~1.7-1.9x prefill throughput and ~1.4-1.7x decode throughput vs our A100 baseline. Raw on-demand token $/1M is ~1.15-1.3x higher on H100, but with kernel tuning + quant profiles the cost gap narrows to ~1.05x for some models.

aj: nice. which models/seq-lens did you run?

maria: ran Llama2-7b, MPT-7B-Instruct, Falcon-7B, each with prefill=512 / decode=512 / batch=8 where applicable. Regions: us-west1 (a100), us-east1 (h100) — tried to keep NVLink config similar.

maria: command (single-node, docker harness):
```
./run_bench --model {llama2-7b,mpt-7b,falcon-7b} \ 
  --gpus a100,h100 --prefill 512 --decode 512 --batch 8 \ 
  --kernels autotune --quant none,bf16,int8 --out csv
```

devin: pasted a very small consolidated table from the csv (units: tok/s and ms where shown)
devin: Llama2-7b — A100: prefill 1,150 tok/s, decode 480 tok/s, median prefill latency 445ms, per-token decode 2.1ms, $/1M tokens: $3.6
devin: Llama2-7b — H100: prefill 2,000 tok/s, decode 760 tok/s, median prefill latency 260ms, per-token decode 1.3ms, $/1M tokens: $4.3
devin: MPT-7B — A100: prefill 980 tok/s, decode 420 tok/s, $/1M tokens: $3.2
devin: MPT-7B — H100: prefill 1,820 tok/s, decode 640 tok/s, $/1M tokens: $3.9
devin: Falcon-7B — A100: prefill 1,020 tok/s, decode 460 tok/s, $/1M tokens: $3.3
devin: Falcon-7B — H100: prefill 1,880 tok/s, decode 690 tok/s, $/1M tokens: $4.0

sasha: interesting — what kernel path was dominant on H100? cutlass/triton/cuBLAS? any custom kernels?

maria: H100 auto-picked a mix: cutlass matmul + our optimized attention kernels (triton-backed). On A100 we saw cuBLAS-heavy path. When we forced the H100 to use cuBLAS-only it lost ~10-12% throughput.

sasha: did you try int8 quant for these? any quality/regression checks?

maria: yes — int8 (PTQ) reduced prefill/decode latency ~22-28% on both GPUs. Quality checks (held-out prompts + perplexity + a small prompt-level evalset) showed small degradation for some instruction prompts, so we only consider int8 for throughput-heavy stateless endpoints.

aj: how much does kernel tuning change cost math?

devin: quick follow — we re-ran Llama2-7b on H100 with tuned kernels and quant profiles. Tuned H100 prefill climbed to 2,100 tok/s and decode 800 tok/s. That shifts $/1M from $4.3 -> $3.95 (est) because TCO dominated by tokens/sec. So tuned H100 ~= 1.1x A100 cost for Llama2-7b instead of 1.2x.

maria: side note: bursty traffic with small seq lengths favors H100 more (lower tail latency). A100 still wins if you do heavy multi-tenant packing where memory footprint -> more instances per host.

bench-bot: [auto] bench: 1769001234 completed — results uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/2026/1769001234/summary.csv

sasha: can you add a short note in the sheet about kernel flags used for the tuned run? we should store the config (cutlass tile sizes, triton grid) with the CSV

maria: yes adding now, and I'll push the perf plots (prefill/decode tok/s, 95p latency, $/1M) to the bench dashboard.

aj: next steps — run a small cluster-level capacity-sizing sim with these numbers (packability factors + region pricing) to see when H100s are cost-justified for customers. I'll spin up a draft.

maria: cool — attaching the quick notes: 1) H100 wins latency & pure throughput; 2) cost gap is tunable via kernels/quant; 3) A100 may be better for high-packing multi-tenant jobs; 4) need end-to-end quality checks before defaulting to int8.

maria: thanks — will link the dashboard here when plots are up :thumbsup:
